template_name: Prediction Error-Dependent Encoding Strength in Architectural Environments

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant generates predictions about upcoming spatial experience based on current context (schematic expectations, visible sightlines, navigational momentum). Predictions are generated in hippocampal CA1 via temporal context model (TCM) dynamics.
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA1 prediction generation; mPFC schema-based expectation

data.finding: Temporal Context Model (TCM): hippocampus maintains a slowly-drifting temporal context that generates predictions about upcoming items/events
data.effect: TCM explains temporal organization of memory

data.finding: Hippocampal CA1 shows prediction-related activity: activation reflects expectation of upcoming events based on current context

justification.backing: Howard's TCM provides the computational framework for how the hippocampus generates predictions based on temporal context. The model explains both the prediction and the encoding enhancement when predictions are violated.
justification.qualifier: TCM is a computational model; the specific implementation in hippocampal circuits is inferred rather than directly observed at the neural level.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial predictions are generated by non-hippocampal systems; but evidence supports hippocampal involvement in spatial prediction.

mechanism_chain.process: When actual spatial experience violates prediction (unexpected view, scale change, material transition, spatial surprise), a prediction error signal is generated. Dopaminergic neurons in VTA respond to novelty/surprise and project to hippocampus.
mechanism_chain.substrate: VTA dopaminergic neurons → hippocampal CA1 via mesolimbic pathway

data.finding: VTA dopaminergic neurons fire to novel or surprising stimuli; novelty-evoked dopamine release in hippocampus enhances plasticity
Prediction error activates mesolimbic dopamine system; dopamine release to hippocampus gates memory encoding

justification.backing: Lisman and Grace established the VTA-hippocampal loop as a mechanism for novelty-enhanced memory encoding. Prediction errors trigger dopamine release that enhances hippocampal plasticity at the moment of surprise.
justification.qualifier: The VTA-hippocampal pathway is established; the specific translation to architectural surprise (scale changes, spatial reveals) is inferred from general novelty research.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if architectural surprises do not activate the same novelty-detection pathway as laboratory stimuli; real-world navigation may habituate to spatial surprises.

mechanism_chain.process: Dopaminergic input to hippocampus enhances synaptic plasticity (LTP) at the moment of prediction error, producing stronger encoding of the surprising spatial experience
mechanism_chain.substrate: D1/D5 receptor activation on CA1 pyramidal neurons → enhanced LTP

data.finding: D1/D5 dopamine receptor activation in CA1 enhances LTP induction and maintenance
Novelty-evoked dopamine in hippocampus produces stronger memory encoding via LTP enhancement

justification.backing: The molecular mechanism linking dopamine to enhanced encoding is well-characterized: D1/D5 receptor activation on CA1 neurons enhances LTP, producing stronger and more durable memory traces for surprising events.
justification.qualifier: The LTP mechanism is established in vitro; the quantitative translation to encoding strength boost (40%) in real environments involves extrapolation.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if in vivo dopamine dynamics differ substantially from slice preparation; or if repeated exposure to the same surprise eliminates the PE signal.

mechanism_chain.process: Prediction error simultaneously creates a discontinuity in the temporal context signal (per TCM), producing an episodic boundary. The surprise is both encoded more strongly AND segments the ongoing experience.
mechanism_chain.substrate: TCM context drift discontinuity; interacts with THRESHOLD_EPISODIC_BOUNDARY_001

data.finding: Event boundaries (including spatial transitions) produce discontinuities in temporal context representation, creating episodic segmentation
Prediction error and episodic boundary encoding share hippocampal mechanisms; both enhance memory for boundary moments

justification.backing: Prediction error and episodic segmentation are linked via TCM: the same context discontinuity that signals surprise also creates an episodic boundary. This produces a double encoding benefit: the surprise is both stronger and more temporally distinctive.
justification.qualifier: The PE-boundary link is established in laboratory paradigms; the specific manifestation in architectural thresholds connects to THRESHOLD_EPISODIC_BOUNDARY_001.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial prediction errors do not produce the same boundary effects as temporal or categorical boundaries; architectural surprise may operate differently.

prediction_error_signal.interpretation: Prediction error encoding boost diminishes after 3–5 repeated exposures to the same surprise; the surprise becomes predicted and the PE signal extinguishes

age_group.effect: Dopaminergic decline in aging reduces VTA → hippocampal PE signal strength; encoding boost from surprise is attenuated (~1.20 rather than 1.40)

anxiety_trait.effect: Anxiety shifts PE processing from curiosity-driven to threat-driven: surprising spatial features are encoded strongly but tagged with negative valence. Amygdala co-activation during PE may produce aversive spatial memories rather than enriching ones.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget state modulates the interpretation of prediction errors. Under allostatic deficit, spatial surprises are more likely to be classified as threats (negative PE) rather than curiosities (positive PE), shifting encoding valence toward aversive. The PE encoding boost still occurs but the memory is tagged with negative affect.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Perceived control determines whether spatial surprises are experienced as delightful (high control: 'I chose to explore this') or disorienting (low control: 'I'm lost and nothing is as expected'). AX4 modulates the valence but not the magnitude of PE encoding.

cross_template_references: THRESHOLD_EPISODIC_BOUNDARY_001 — PE at thresholds produces episodic segmentation
ED_HIPPOCAMPAL_ENCODING_001 — PE boost operates on top of base encoding strength
ED_SCHEMA_ENCODING_001 — schema violation IS prediction error; these templates share the same mechanism
NEUROMOD-I (Schultz) — dopaminergic PE mechanism overlaps; avoid double-counting when NEUROMOD-I panel calibrates reward PE

nature_view_quality.interpretation: The degree of unexpected spatial expansion or contraction at a transition point; larger reveals produce larger PE

environmental_novelty_level.interpretation: More predictable spatial sequences produce LOWER PE encoding; monotonous corridors with identical segments suppress PE signal
